Lailashi Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lailashi, Georgia

Not demolished. Settled by Jewish refugees fleeing persecution in Akhaltsikhe after a 17th-century Turkish invasion, Lailashi grew into the largest Jewish settlement in Western Georgia, reaching roughly 1,200 people — the majority of the village — in the early 20th century. Its synagogue once held the extraordinary Lailashi Bible, a Torah manuscript dated to the 10th or 11th century, with a local legend claiming it was carried to Georgia by angels and found floating in a river; the manuscript, believed to hold miraculous powers, was revered by both Jews and Georgians and is now preserved at the Georgian National Centre of Manuscripts. This older of Lailashi's two Jewish cemeteries predates its 'new' counterpart, though its gravestones are now too illegible to date; the last Jews left the village by the 1970s, and today the site is used as a backyard agricultural plot, its remaining tombstones reduced to a scattered pile of broken stone.
